paragraphs.title: The Lord Challenges Job About the Secrets of Creation

easy.explanation: Job 38:1 says that the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind.
easy.q: From where did the LORD answer Job?

easy.explanation: The LORD asked who darkened counsel by words without knowledge.
easy.q: What did the LORD say Job was darkening?

answers: Gird up his loins like a man
easy.explanation: Job was told to gird up his loins and prepare to answer.
easy.q: What did the LORD command Job to do?

answers: The LORD would question him and require an answer
Job was about to travel through the wilderness
Job needed to control the sea
medium.explanation: The LORD said He would demand of Job, and Job was to answer Him.
medium.q: Why was Job told to gird up his loins?

answers: The foundations and mysteries of creation
medium.explanation: The following questions concern the earth, heavens, sea, and other parts of creation.
medium.q: What subject would Job be questioned about?

answers: A song sung by the morning stars
A command given to the sea
medium.explanation: The phrase describes words spoken without sufficient knowledge or understanding.
medium.q: What does the phrase “words without knowledge” mean in context?

answers: He becomes a king over creation
He becomes the one being questioned rather than the questioner
He receives power over the whirlwind
challenge.explanation: The LORD takes the role of the questioner and requires Job to answer.
challenge.q: How does Job’s position change at the beginning of the LORD’s speech?

answers: Job is challenged to demonstrate whether he truly understands
Job is commanded to remain silent
Job is given the secrets of creation
challenge.explanation: The wording challenges Job to show whether he possesses the needed understanding.
challenge.q: What does “declare, if thou hast understanding” imply?

answers: Human beings fully understand the universe
Job’s limited knowledge is placed before God’s questions
Job has authority over the natural world
challenge.explanation: The LORD’s questions expose the limits of Job’s knowledge.
challenge.q: What central idea is established by these opening verses?

paragraphs.title: The Foundations of Earth and the Song of Heaven

easy.explanation: The LORD asks where Job was when He laid the foundations of the earth.
easy.q: What does the LORD first ask Job about?

easy.explanation: The LORD asks who stretched the line upon the earth.
easy.q: What was stretched upon the earth?

easy.explanation: The verse says that all the sons of God shouted for joy.
easy.q: Who shouted for joy when the earth was founded?

medium.explanation: The passage refers to the earth’s measures, foundations, and corner stone.
medium.q: Which details about the earth are mentioned together?

medium.explanation: Job 38:7 says that the morning stars sang together.
medium.q: What did the morning stars do when the earth was founded?

medium.explanation: The line is imagery for measuring and establishing the earth.
medium.q: In “Who hath stretched the line upon it?”, what does “line” most likely describe?

answers: To show that Job created the earth
To emphasize that Job did not witness or establish its foundations
challenge.explanation: The questions test whether Job was present and understood the earth’s founding.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the LORD’s questions about the earth?

answers: It presents creation as a joyful heavenly event
It describes a battle on earth
It proves that the stars were measured by Job
challenge.explanation: The singing stars and rejoicing sons of God give the event a celebratory character.
challenge.q: What does the singing of the morning stars add to the description?

answers: The earth’s physical foundations and heaven’s joyful response
challenge.explanation: The passage joins the establishment of earth with heavenly rejoicing.
challenge.q: What contrast appears in this passage?

answers: As coming forth from the womb
easy.explanation: The sea is pictured as breaking forth as if it had issued out of the womb.
easy.q: How is the sea described when it first appears in the passage?

easy.explanation: The cloud was its garment, and thick darkness was its swaddlingband.
easy.q: What did the LORD make the garment and swaddlingband of the sea?

easy.explanation: The LORD set bars and doors and established a limit for the sea.
easy.q: What restrained the proud waves of the sea?

medium.explanation: The sea comes forth, is covered, and is then given a boundary.
medium.q: What sequence describes the sea in this passage?

answers: To picture the sea being restrained
To open the gates of death
medium.explanation: Bars and doors illustrate the boundary that keeps the sea in place.
medium.q: Why are bars and doors mentioned?

answers: Rods or barriers used to close something
medium.explanation: Bars are closing or restraining devices, reinforcing the image of confinement.
medium.q: In context, what does “bars” mean?

answers: The sea is part of the created order under God’s authority
challenge.explanation: The image presents the sea as something brought forth and governed by God.
challenge.q: What does the image of the sea coming from the womb suggest?

answers: The sea has a clearly appointed limit
challenge.explanation: The LORD gives the sea a definite boundary that it cannot pass.
challenge.q: What does “Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further” emphasize?

answers: The powerful sea remains subject to divine order and restraint
challenge.explanation: The sea’s proud waves are stopped by the boundary appointed by the LORD.
challenge.q: What main idea emerges from the passage?

paragraphs.title: Light, Dawn, Darkness, and the Limits of Knowledge

answers: Whether he had commanded the morning
Whether he had fed the lions
Whether he had founded the earth
easy.explanation: The LORD asks whether Job had commanded the morning and shown the dayspring its place.
easy.q: What does the LORD ask Job about at the beginning of this passage?

answers: It takes hold of the earth and shakes the wicked out
easy.explanation: The passage pictures the light as shaking the wicked out of the earth.
easy.q: What does the morning do to the earth?

answers: The gates of death and the doors of the shadow of death
easy.explanation: The LORD asks whether Job has seen the gates of death and the doors of the shadow of death.
easy.q: Which gates are mentioned in the passage?

answers: Dawn exposes and shakes them out
Dawn hides them from the light
Dawn invites them toward the sea
medium.explanation: The morning light is portrayed as bringing judgment and exposure.
medium.q: What is the relationship between dawn and the wicked in the passage?

answers: The deep, death, the earth, light, and darkness
medium.explanation: The questions cover the earth, the deep, death, light, and darkness.
medium.q: Which areas of knowledge does the LORD ask Job about?

answers: A dark realm associated with death
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a mysterious and deeply dark region connected with death.
medium.q: What does “the shadow of death” describe in context?

answers: To test whether Job knows the paths and dwelling place of light
To teach Job how to light a fire
challenge.explanation: The LORD questions whether Job understands where light and darkness belong.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of asking, “Where is the way where light dwelleth?”

answers: Job controls the length of his life
Job does not even possess complete knowledge of his own life
Job knows the number of everyone’s days
challenge.explanation: The question highlights Job’s limited knowledge of his own beginning and lifespan.
challenge.q: What does the question about Job’s birth and the number of his days imply?

answers: Job is questioned about realities he does not control
Job is asked to teach the stars
Job is asked to stop the waves
challenge.explanation: Even basic cosmic processes are presented as beyond Job’s command.
challenge.q: How are light and dawn connected to the limits of knowledge?

paragraphs.title: Storehouses of Snow, Rain, Ice, and Desert Growth

answers: The storehouses of snow and hail
The storehouses of gold and silver
The storehouses of bread and water
easy.explanation: The passage mentions the treasures, or storehouses, of snow and hail.
easy.q: Which storehouses does the LORD ask Job whether he has entered?

answers: On land where no man is and on the wilderness
easy.explanation: The rain falls even where no human being lives.
easy.q: Where does the rain fall according to the passage?

answers: They are hidden as with a stone and the deep is frozen
easy.explanation: The waters are described as hidden and the face of the deep as frozen.
easy.q: What happens to the waters in the description of ice?

answers: Satisfy it and cause tender plants to spring forth
medium.explanation: Rain satisfies the desolate ground and causes the tender herb to grow.
medium.q: What can rain do for desolate ground?

answers: They are reserved for a time of trouble and a day of battle and war
They are used to build weapons
medium.explanation: The LORD says these storehouses are reserved against trouble, battle, and war.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between snow, hail, and battle?

answers: New growth coming from a plant
medium.explanation: The word refers to the fresh growth of a tender plant.
medium.q: In “cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth,” what does “bud” refer to?

answers: God’s provision is not limited to inhabited places
Rain falls only where Job is present
challenge.explanation: The passage shows rain being sent even to places without human inhabitants.
challenge.q: What does rain falling in a wilderness where no man is emphasize?

answers: Water brings growth in the desert and can also become ice
challenge.explanation: Rain produces vegetation, while cold turns water into ice.
challenge.q: What relationship between water, life, and freezing appears in the passage?

answers: They test whether Job directs complex natural processes
They explain the lives of angels
challenge.explanation: The LORD asks whether Job knows or controls the sources and operations of these phenomena.
challenge.q: What do the questions about rain, hail, and ice have in common?

paragraphs.title: The Systems and Laws of Heaven

easy.explanation: The LORD asks whether Job can bind the influences of Pleiades or loose Orion’s bands.
easy.q: Which star groups are named in the passage?

answers: Whether he can bring it forth in its season
Whether he can hide it in the sea
easy.explanation: Job is asked whether he can bring forth Mazzaroth in its season.
easy.q: What does the LORD ask Job about Mazzaroth?

easy.explanation: The passage asks whether Job can lift his voice to the clouds and send lightnings.
easy.q: What else is Job asked whether he can command?

answers: They belong to an ordered system with appointed times
They belong to the animal world
medium.explanation: The passage refers to seasons, ordinances, and dominion in the heavens.
medium.q: What do the questions about stars and constellations suggest?

answers: They answer to the one who can command them
They create the earth by themselves
medium.explanation: The question asks whether Job can call the clouds and send lightnings at his command.
medium.q: What is the relationship between clouds, lightning, and authority?

medium.explanation: Dominion refers to rule, authority, or governing order.
medium.q: What does “dominion thereof” mean in “canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth?”

answers: The LORD governs heaven, while Job is questioned about whether he can do so
Job governs the stars while the LORD merely observes
challenge.explanation: The LORD’s questions present heavenly order as beyond Job’s control.
challenge.q: What contrast do the questions create between the LORD and Job?

answers: Job is asked whether he can establish heavenly dominion in the earth
Heaven and earth have no relationship
The earth cancels the ordinances of heaven
challenge.explanation: The verse joins the ordinances of heaven with the question of setting their dominion in earth.
challenge.q: What relationship between heaven and earth is suggested?

answers: Star groups, constellations, clouds, lightning, and rain
Lions, ravens, the sea, and snow
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from heavenly bodies to clouds, lightning, and abundant waters.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly summarizes the areas of control mentioned?

paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Care for Wild Animals and the Raven

easy.explanation: The LORD asks whether Job hunts prey for the lion.
easy.q: Which animal is mentioned first in this passage?

answers: In their dens and covert places
easy.explanation: The young lions couch in their dens and abide in covert places.
easy.q: Where do the young lions lie in wait?

easy.explanation: The verse says that the young ravens cry unto God.
easy.q: To whom do the young ravens cry when they lack food?

answers: Job is not the one who provides their food
They both live in the sea
medium.explanation: The LORD asks whether Job provides prey for lions or food for the raven’s young.
medium.q: What do the lions and ravens have in common in this passage?

answers: They cry unto God and wander for lack of meat
medium.explanation: The verse describes their cry to God and their wandering because they lack food.
medium.q: What happens to the young ravens when they lack food?

medium.explanation: Prey is an animal captured and eaten by another animal.
medium.q: What does “prey” mean in “Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion?”

answers: To show that Job does not control the needs of wild animals
To teach Job how to build a trap
To describe the foundations of the earth
challenge.explanation: The final questions show that Job does not provide food for wild creatures.
challenge.q: Why does the passage end with lions and ravens?

answers: The needs of animals are presented within God’s providential care
Job must raise every young bird
challenge.explanation: Their cry points to God as the one associated with their provision.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the young ravens crying unto God?

answers: The focus moves from heavenly powers to the feeding of animals
The focus moves from the sea to the foundations of earth
The focus moves only from light to the gates of death
challenge.explanation: The passage concludes by moving from cosmic order to the practical needs of living creatures.
challenge.q: What conceptual movement occurs at the end of the passage?
